newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: Papua New Guinean PM Chan in danger of losing seat.
newsitem.headline: Papua New Guinean PM Chan in danger of losing seat.

text.p: Papua New Guinea's early polling results released on Sunday show controversial Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan will struggle to hold his seat in parliament.

Chan was forced to temporarily step aside from the prime ministership this year after civil unrest over a government attempt to quell a rebellion with mercenaries. He trails his rival by 732 votes with more than a third of the vote counted.
Chan will not retain the prime ministership if he loses the vote.

Papua New Guinea's Electoral Commission said after votes had been counted from 17 of the total 46 ballot boxes in the seat of Namata Nai, Chan had received 2,464 votes while his rival Ephraim Apelis had received 3,196 votes.

Chan has been an unpopular figure in Papua New Guinea since March when it emerged he was behind a US$36 million deal to hire African mercenaries to quash a secessionist rebellion on the copper-rich island of Bougainville.

The revelations sparked an army mutiny. Senior army officers said they were fed up with corruption and called for the government to resign. Civilians rioted for two days before Chan resigned as prime minister while an official inquiry was held.
Chan reclaimed the prime-ministership in early June, saying the inquiry had cleared him.
The remainder of votes in the electorate, which Chan has held since Papua New Guinea was granted independence from Australia in 1975, are expected to be counted by Monday morning.
Voting in national elections in the the South Pacific nation of 4.3 million people began on June 12 and finished on Saturday. The final results will be officially declared on July 15.
